about: Grind Strat's own drawn shapes for the dated map (M3a): the Vistula Lagoon's old outlets and today's Pillau strait, Ruden and its lost land bridge to Rügen, a larger Lake Drużno, and the Vistula delta's marsh before diking. Each is our own reconstruction ('reconstructed'), drawn in longitude and latitude on public-domain heights and land and on published coordinates, then moved onto the game's map with MAP.toUnits (tools/map/projection.mjs) and rounded to whole game units (100 m). None is traced from OpenStreetMap or from any map still in copyright. tools/map/pack-changes.mjs packs them into src/data/own/changes.json; tools/map/water-changes.json dates them (its 'shape' fields) and holds the sources named here.

fields.id: the shape id that tools/map/water-changes.json names
fields.type: 'water' (a channel cut through the base land: drawn as sea or lagoon water), 'land' (land over today's sea), 'lake' (a lake drawn over the land), 'terrain' (land cells with a class of their own for a while: the land engine's overrides)
fields.class: terrain only: the class the cells hold ('marsh')
fields.ring: the outline, [x, y] in game units (100 m) on the game map, first point not repeated (the packer turns it counter-clockwise)
fields.drawnFrom: what it was drawn on and from

shapes.drawnFrom: a 400 m channel across the land between the sea and the lagoon's north-east tip, just south-west of Lochstedt castle (54.7070N 19.9513E, German Wikipedia), placed on the GEBCO_2026 heights and sea depths (public domain; the native 15 arc-second grid, read for drawing only); cut through the base land (Natural Earth 1:10m, public domain)

a 400 m channel across the spit north-west of Frombork (54.35N 19.68E, Wikipedia), across the narrowest dune ridge on the GEBCO_2026 heights and sea depths (public domain; the native 15 arc-second grid, read for drawing only); cut through the base land (Natural Earth 1:10m, public domain)

a 400 m channel across the spit north-west of Balga (54.5525N 19.9694E, Wikipedia), across the dune ridge on the GEBCO_2026 heights and sea depths (public domain; the native 15 arc-second grid, read for drawing only); cut through the base land (Natural Earth 1:10m, public domain)

a 400 m channel (today's strait is about 400 m wide, Wikipedia) along the deep cells through the spit at the strait's published point (54.6411N 19.8783E, Wikipedia) on the GEBCO_2026 heights and sea depths (public domain; the native 15 arc-second grid, read for drawing only); cut through the base land (Natural Earth 1:10m, public domain), which has no strait

an island 2.3 km long and about 400 m wide (German Wikipedia) round the land cells GEBCO shows at 54.20-54.21N 13.77E (the GEBCO_2026 heights and sea depths (public domain; the native 15 arc-second grid, read for drawing only)); not in the base land (Natural Earth 1:10m, public domain)

a 500 m strip from Ruden's north end to the south tip of Mönchgut by Thiessow (54.2769N 13.7122E, German Wikipedia), along the shallowest cells between them on the GEBCO_2026 heights and sea depths (public domain; the native 15 arc-second grid, read for drawing only); its course and width are a guess

the low ground below about 0 m between Elbląg and today's lake, along the foot of the Elbląg upland on the GEBCO_2026 heights and sea depths (public domain; the native 15 arc-second grid, read for drawing only), sized after the lake's 13th-century range in Nitychoruk et al. (2016), Text-fig. 9 (a picture we looked at; not traced, as it is not out of copyright)

the Vistula delta's low ground, outlined by hand on the GEBCO_2026 heights and sea depths (public domain; the native 15 arc-second grid, read for drawing only): the foot of the uplands round Gdańsk, Tczew, Malbork and Elbląg, the coast and the lagoon's south-west end; the 1 km cells inside it are those on the base land (Natural Earth 1:10m, public domain) whose height (the base block's 2 km heights) is 5 m or less, and the lowest (0 m or less) are the second wave
